sections.html:
Everything happens in Bedford, and all three offices have Highway 42 East addresses. The PVA values each parcel at fair cash value under KRS 132.450 and keeps the roll that every taxing district bills from.

Trimble County tax offices in Bedford
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
PVA, values property107 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 131(502) 255-35928:30 to 4:30, shut 12:00 to 12:30
Sheriff, takes payment30 Hwy 42 E(502) 255-71388:00 to 4:30
County Clerk, deeds and late bills30 Hwy 42 E, PO Box 262(502) 255-71748:30 to 4:30

All three keep weekday hours only. The sheriff's office also handles patrols, vehicle inspections and court security, so ring ahead when you need a payoff letter for a closing date.

Trimble is one of the smallest Kentucky counties by land, about 152 square miles, with the Ohio River as its western boundary facing Indiana. Bedford, the seat, sits at the junction of US 421 and US 42. Milton, at US 421 and KY 36 facing Madison, Indiana, is the oldest and largest town. Smaller places include Wises Landing, Providence, Monitor and Mount Pleasant. The Trimble County Generating Station, on 2,200 acres beside the river about 50 miles from Louisville, is the best known industrial site.

The population grew 33.4 percent in the 1990s to 8,125, peaked at 8,809 in 2010 and slipped to 8,474 by the 2020 count. It is now estimated at 8,701, which is 2.7 percent above the April 2020 base. Housing looks like this:

  • Homes lived in by their owners: 79.7 percent, with 3,931 housing units in all.
  • Typical home value: $172,000. Typical rent: $863 a month.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,286 with a mortgage and $420 without one.
  • Households: 3,382 at 2.52 people each, with 93.6 percent of residents in the same house a year before.

Most owners stay put for years, so listings tend to come from long-time residents, heirs or landlords.

sections.h2: The state share of your bill
sections.html:
For 2025 the Commonwealth's rate is 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessed value, down a notch from 10.9 cents. County, school and district levies sit on top of that figure, and the sheriff can quote the combined rate for any parcel.

A homeowner with the $49,100 age or disability exemption is billed on the assessed value minus that amount, which lowers every levy applied to it. A 2 percent prompt payment discount trims the whole bill, not just the state's slice.

One calendar governs the sheriff, written into KRS 134.015.

  • Through November 1: the bill is cut by 2 percent.
  • November 2 to December 31: the printed amount.
  • January: 5 percent is added.
  • February onward: 10 percent is added, along with the sheriff's own fee.

When April 15 closes, whatever is still open moves from the sheriff to the clerk. The clerk records a lien on the parcel, interest of one percent a month begins, and the clerk and county attorney earn commissions. Paying quickly after the handoff avoids part of the cost.

Two attorney letters follow, the second naming the sale date, and an advertisement runs a month or more before. No sale can be held until 90 days after the handoff. A lien can survive 11 years and follows the land, so a title agent will not close over it. Get the Trimble County Clerk's exact payoff and let closing funds cover it.

Start by phoning the PVA, because a meeting with that office is the gate to any appeal. Each year the roll is on public view for thirteen days, starting the first Monday of May. Anyone still unhappy then files at the clerk's office, no later than the day after viewing ends.

Local owners sit as the panel, 25 to 35 days after viewing. Only proof shown in front of the PVA or a deputy counts, so bring photos, repair estimates, insurance papers and nearby sales. The panel writes down any change it makes, and the hearing may be recorded. When the final figure ends up higher than the one you claimed, a supplemental bill covers the gap.

Owners who have reached 65 qualify, as do owners whom a federal agency or retirement system has classed as totally disabled. The deduction is $49,100 across 2025 and 2026. Hand the form to the PVA at 107 Hwy 42 E along with proof of age.

Anyone claiming on disability must reapply each year. The exceptions are owners whose disability came from military service and owners that Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled. About 21.4 percent of Trimble residents are 65 or older, so a good share of owners may be able to use it.

sections.h2: Paperwork to line up before closing
sections.html:
Tax status and the deed are the two gating items. The clerk's office on Highway 42 records the deed. Kentucky wants mailing addresses for both parties, the full price, an in care of address for that year's tax bill and a sworn certificate that the price is true. It must also cite how the seller took title.

  • Get what is owed in writing from the sheriff.
  • Ask the clerk whether any delinquent bill has been recorded against the parcel.
  • Tell the PVA about the sale if an exemption was on file.
  • Write the buyer's own mailing address into the deed for next year's bill.

Back taxes, a vacant inherited house or a tenant in poor repair do not have to be fixed before selling. A cash buyer will take the house as is and pay the balance from the proceeds.

The usual order is simple. Call the sheriff at (502) 255-7138 for this year's balance, then the clerk at (502) 255-7174 for anything that has been recorded as delinquent. Put both numbers in front of the closing agent. If the lien is older, expect it to be paid from your proceeds before you receive anything.

An owner who wants to skip showings and repairs can compare a cash offer against a listing by the amount left after payoffs, not by the price alone. Ask any buyer who will pay recording costs and how soon they can close.

Bring a photo ID and the parcel number to each office, and ask for each figure in writing with the date it was calculated. Interest runs monthly on a delinquent bill, so a number from close to closing day is the one a title agent will use. If you inherited the house, bring papers showing who has authority to sign the deed. Doing this a couple of weeks ahead leaves room for a second visit if an office needs something more.

faqs.q: Which Trimble County office takes my tax payment?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office does, at 30 Hwy 42 E in Bedford, phone (502) 255-7138. The PVA down the road at number 107 only values property, and the clerk handles bills after they turn delinquent.

faqs.q: What are the hours at the Trimble County PVA?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, except a lunch closing from 12:00 to 12:30. The phone number is (502) 255-3592.

faqs.q: Is Bedford the largest town in Trimble County?
faqs.a: No, Milton is the largest town, while Bedford is the county seat. Milton stands on the Ohio River at US 421 and KY 36, across from Madison, Indiana.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Trimble County home worth?
faqs.a: The middle value for 2020 to 2024 is $172,000. Median rent is $863 a month, and owners live in 79.7 percent of homes.

faqs.q: Does a delinquent Trimble County tax bill disappear if I sell?
faqs.a: No. The lien rides with the parcel for as long as 11 years, so someone has to pay it by closing day. The County Clerk's office can give you the figure.
